title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)
body: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is a form of public-key cryptography based on the algebraic structure of elliptic curves over finite fields. ECC allows for smaller key sizes compared to non-EC cryptography (based on plain Galois fields) while providing an equivalent level of security.

This project explores the mathematical foundations of ECC — including point addition, scalar multiplication, and the discrete logarithm problem over elliptic curves — and implements a simulator that demonstrates key exchange and digital signatures using standard curves.
